主要内容: The U.S. Department of the Treasury announced its intent to fully exit its investment in General Motors (GM) within the next 12-15 months, subject to market conditions. As of December 19, 2012, the Treasury held 500.1 million shares of GM common stock. The plan involves GM purchasing 200 million shares at $27.50 per share, expected to close by the end of 2012. The remaining 300.1 million shares will be sold through various means in an orderly fashion over the next 12-15 months, starting as early as January 2013. Treasury has recovered more than $28.7 billion of its investment in GM through repayments, sales, dividends, and other income. The Treasury also noted that the auto industry rescue helped save over a million jobs during the 2008-2009 economic crisis. The Treasury emphasized that TARP was always intended to be a temporary program, and the exit from GM aligns with its goals of winding down TARP and protecting taxpayer interests.
